stories.title: Higher Treasury yields give a hot economy a reality check
stories.summary: Treasury yields have climbed, and analysts say the move is a reality check for an economy that is running hot and prone to inflation. Higher yields raise borrowing costs across the economy. The rise adds pressure on the Fed as it weighs its next move.
stories.whyItMatters: Rising yields ripple into mortgages, loans, and stock valuations, so this move touches nearly every corner of the market.
whatToWatch: Further moves in Treasury yields
The Fed's response to inflation pressure
Effects on borrowing costs economy-wide
questions: How high will yields climb before the Fed acts?
Will inflation data confirm the hot-economy read?

sources.title: Analysis: Higher Treasury yields deliver a reality check on a hot, inflation-prone economy

stories.title: Surging Treasury yields create a new problem for Kevin Warsh and the Fed
stories.summary: Treasury yields have surged, creating a fresh challenge for Kevin Warsh and the Federal Reserve. The report frames this as a new complication in the Fed's policy path. No further detail on the size or cause of the surge is given in the source.
stories.whyItMatters: Yield surges complicate Fed decision-making and can shift expectations for rate policy, which moves stock and bond markets.
whatToWatch: Any Fed commentary responding to the yield surge
Kevin Warsh's public statements on policy
questions: What specifically is driving the surge in yields?

stories.whyItMatters: Small caps are sensitive to borrowing costs, so a bond sell-off can hit them harder than large-cap stocks.

stories.title: 30-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2004
stories.summary: The 30-year Treasury yield has hit its highest level since 2004, CNBC reports, as a bond market rout continues. The move extends a broader sell-off in Treasuries. The source does not give the exact yield level.
stories.whyItMatters: A multi-decade high in long-term yields raises borrowing costs across mortgages, corporate debt, and government financing.
whatToWatch: Whether the 30-year yield climbs further
Any policy response from the Fed or Treasury
questions: What is driving the rout, and how long could it last?

stories.summary: A Citi survey finds family offices are doubling down on stocks and private equity, even as inflation stokes worry, CNBC reports. The finding suggests wealthy investors remain willing to take on risk. No further detail on allocation size is given.
stories.whyItMatters: Family office positioning offers a read on how sophisticated, long-horizon investors view current market risk.
whatToWatch: Further Citi survey findings on family office allocations
Whether inflation concerns change this positioning

stories.title: Oracle stock falls after force majeure notice on data-center project
stories.summary: Oracle shares fell about 3% after the company sent a force majeure notice regarding a data-center project, according to CNBC and MarketWatch. Investors reacted to fears of a setback in Oracle's data-center buildout. Neither source gives further detail on the cause of the notice.
stories.whyItMatters: Oracle's data-center capacity underpins its AI cloud business, so a delay could raise doubts about its growth plans.
whatToWatch: Oracle's next update on the affected data-center project
Analyst reaction to the force majeure notice
questions: What caused the force majeure notice?
How much will this delay Oracle's data-center plans?

stories.title: Fed seeks public comment on stablecoin issuer rules under GENIUS Act
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve Board has requested public comment on two proposals to set up a regulatory framework for Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers, under the GENIUS Act. The proposals mark a step toward formal oversight of stablecoin issuers. The release does not detail the comment period length.
stories.whyItMatters: Formal stablecoin rules would shape how crypto-linked payment firms operate under Fed oversight, a significant shift for digital-asset markets.
whatToWatch: The public comment period and deadline
Final rules once the Fed reviews comments
questions: How will these proposals affect existing stablecoin issuers?
